name: Indian Ocean
genZNote: India isn't just a country ON the Indian Ocean — it sits right in the middle of it, like the whole ocean is named after the one country that can't avoid it. Geography flex, honestly.

sections.heading: 🌊 Location & Extent
bullets: The third-largest ocean, bounded by Africa to the west, Asia to the north, and Australia to the east, opening into the Southern Ocean below.
The only major ocean named after a single country — a reflection of India's central position within it, not a claim of ownership.
Unlike the Pacific and Atlantic, it is mostly closed off in the north by the Asian landmass, which shapes its unique monsoon-driven current system.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Countries With Coastlines On It
bullets: East Africa: Somalia, Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, South Africa's Indian Ocean coast, and island nations Madagascar, Mauritius, Seychelles.
Middle East: Oman, Yemen (via the Arabian Sea/Gulf of Aden), the UAE and other Gulf states (via the Arabian Sea).
South Asia: India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Maldives.
Southeast Asia: Indonesia, Thailand, Myanmar (via the Bay of Bengal and Andaman Sea).
Australia's western and southern coasts.

sections.heading: 🌐 Connected Seas & Notable Features
bullets: Major connected seas: Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, Red Sea (via the Gulf of Aden), Andaman Sea.
The only ocean with a fully monsoon-reversing current system — surface currents flip direction seasonally with the monsoon winds, unlike any other ocean.
Major island groups: Madagascar, Sri Lanka, the Maldives, the Seychelles, and India's own Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep islands.
The Strait of Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb sit at its northwestern edges, and the Strait of Malacca at its eastern edge — three of the world's most strategically important chokepoints.

sections.heading: 🚢 Trade & Strategic Importance
bullets: Carries a huge share of the world's oil trade — tankers from the Gulf pass through the Strait of Hormuz and across the Arabian Sea toward Asia, Europe and beyond.
The main sea route between Europe and East Asia runs through it, via the Red Sea/Suez Canal on one end and the Strait of Malacca on the other.
For India specifically, the Indian Ocean carries the majority of its trade by volume — energy imports from the Gulf, and exports/imports with East Africa, Southeast Asia and beyond.
The Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) is the main regional cooperation body built around this ocean, with India as a key member.

sections.heading: 🐠 Marine Ecology & Environmental Concerns
bullets: Home to extensive coral reef systems around the Maldives, Lakshadweep, Sri Lanka and the Red Sea, along with mangrove belts across the Sundarbans (India/Bangladesh) and East Africa.
Warming waters have caused repeated coral bleaching events in the Maldives, Lakshadweep and around the Chagos Archipelago.
Monsoon-driven upwelling supports major fisheries along the Arabian Sea coast and off East Africa.
Rising sea levels are a direct existential concern for low-lying island nations in this ocean, especially the Maldives.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Indian Ocean is Earth's third-largest ocean, bounded by Africa, Asia and Australia, with India at its geographic and strategic centre.
keyFacts: Third-largest ocean; only ocean named after one country.
Only ocean with a fully monsoon-reversing current system.
Major connected seas: Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, Red Sea (via Gulf of Aden), Andaman Sea.
IORA (Indian Ocean Rim Association) is the key regional body.
commonConfusion: The Indian Ocean isn't "India's ocean" territorially — it's simply named for India's central position; many countries share its coastline and trade routes.

highYieldFacts: Third-largest ocean; borders Africa, Asia, Australia; opens south into the Southern Ocean.
Only ocean with monsoon-reversing surface currents.
Three critical chokepoints sit at its edges: Hormuz, Bab-el-Mandeb, Malacca.
commonTraps: Don't assume every East African or Southeast Asian country borders the Indian Ocean directly — some connect only through a marginal sea.
IORA is a cooperation body, not a defence alliance — don't confuse it with the Quad.
mustRemember: Indian Ocean = 3rd largest; India-centred; monsoon currents; Hormuz + Bab-el-Mandeb + Malacca at its edges.
